channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Rate spread outlook favors JPY against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that JPY is underperforming as firmer Oil prices support USD/JPY, while the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) latest meeting minutes did little to shift rate expectations.

item.title: Gold holds firm as Fed rate outlook, Middle East developments remain in focus
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles to extend gains on Monday as buyers take a breather following last week’s sharp rally, with the broader market theme still centred on the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest-rate outlook and developments in the Middle East.

item.title: Copper: Weak China imports contrast with bullish positioning - ING
item.description: ING strategists Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson highlight that China’s latest trade data show continued weakness in copper imports, with unwrought volumes down 11.5% year-on-year and concentrate flows also softer.

item.title: US Dollar: Higher hurdle for sustained gains – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes that weaker US jobs data have not triggered a strong reaction in Dollar or rates, as markets await key Consumer Price Index (CPI) releases and another Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) before the September Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).

item.title: Euro: Modest upside bias against US Dollar as Fed repricing – Rabobank
item.description: Rabıobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses recent EUR/USD strength, noting it was mainly driven by a softer Dollar after weak United States (US) labour data reduced Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike expectations.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA policy pause maintained – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to leave the cash rate unchanged at 4.35%, noting that policy is already restrictive and that Australian activity, particularly housing, is slowing in response to earlier hikes.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ tightening risks support JPY – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Wee Khoon Chong highlights that long-end JGB yields are rising on inflation and fiscal concerns, with markets pricing a roughly 50% chance of a 25bp BoJ hike in September and a full hike by year-end.

item.title: Oil: Strait risk and cautious positioning – ING
item.description: ING analysts Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson note that Oil prices remain supported by uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran negotiations continue.

item.title: Silver tests $65: Why are buyers struggling to extend the rally?
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) struggles to extend its gains on Monday following last week’s strong breakout as traders assess the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest rate outlook amid risks on both sides of its dual mandate.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Rate hike odds slashed after soft inflation – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that Norwegian Krone (NOK) is trading mixed as firmer Oil offsets the drag from reduced Norges Bank tightening expectations.

item.title: Canadian Dollar steadies, caught between risk aversion, rebounding Oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.3940 on Monday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day after falling sharply on Friday.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed pricing shifts with softer data – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists note that Friday’s mixed United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report led to a notable repricing of September Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) odds, with futures-implied probability of a hike falling to 44%.

item.title: Australian Dollar approaches two-month highs at 0.7088 with RBA decision on tap
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) holds gains, in the mid-range of the 0.7000s against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, with two-month highs of 0.7088 at hand. The Aussie is capitalising on the US Dollar’s weakness, as hopes of Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hikes wane.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: On verge of downward-trendline breakout
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades slightly lower at around 1.1550 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Monday.

item.title: Federal Reserve: September hike odds reassessed – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Bas van Geffen comments that weaker United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) and a drop in labour supply have reduced urgency for another Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike, though policy remains data‑dependent.

item.title: Copper: Tariff-driven arbitrage reshapes COMEX-LME spread – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem argue that Copper has shifted into a policy-driven trade as Section 232 tariffs reshape the COMEX-LME arbitrage.

item.title: Japanese Yen underperforms on surprising current account deficit
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) is down against its major currency peers on Monday, trading 0.6% lower at around 158.80 against the US Dollar (USD) at the time of writing during the European trading session.

item.title: Gold: Central bank demand underpins rally – ING
item.description: ING’s Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson report that Gold extended its rally as the People’s Bank of China (PBoC) added 640koz to reserves, marking 21 consecutive months of accumulation. Spot Gold moved above $4,320/oz, supported by ongoing central bank buying and stronger Chinese ETF demand.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD remains bullish, pushing against $4,380 resistance
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) holds moderate gains at the mid-range of the $4,300s on Monday, consolidating gains after a nearly 7.5% rally last week.

item.title: US Dollar: Softer labor data supports downside – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu and David Tam note that weaker United States (US) labor data have lowered real-rate expectations and extended the Dollar decline, creating a more supportive environment for risk assets and duration.

item.title: Indian Rupee falls as Iran tightens Hormuz reopening conditions
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) is down against the US Dollar (USD) at the start of the week. The USD/INR pair rebounds to near 95.30 as oil prices extend their recovery move and the US Dollar regains ground after a weak Friday.

item.title: Experts agree: The US Dollar rally migh have come to an end
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) consolidates losses, trading below 100.00 at the time of writing on Monday, holding near its lowest levels since mid-June.

item.title: British Pound tests 1.3500 as US Dollar struggles to shake off NFP shock
item.description: GBP/USD trades around 1.3495 on Monday at the time of writing, up a modest 0.04% on the day. However, the pair struggles to hold firmly above the psychological 1.3500 level after benefiting on Friday from a decline in the US Dollar (USD) triggered by disappointing United States (US) employment data.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Policy hold guidance in focus – Nomura
item.description: Nomura’s Josie Anderson, George Buckley and Andrzej Szczepaniak expect Norges Bank to keep its policy rate at 4.25% at the August meeting, citing softer underlying inflation and benign domestic data.

item.title: CEE FX: Data-heavy week under global pressure – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky highlights a busy Central and Eastern Europe calendar with Czech inflation, Turkey’s inflation report and key Polish data, including GDP and core inflation.

item.title: Euro: Fed repricing supports gains against US Dollar – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists highlight that EUR/USD has squeezed above key resistance as Dollar weakness follows softer United States (US) employment data and reduced odds of a September Fed hike. The pair is seen slightly expensive versus nat gas but near fair value on 2-year spreads.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Hawkish RBA hold supports carry – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes that the Australian Dollar (AUD) remains one of the most attractive G10 currencies thanks to favorable carry and a hawkish Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $64.24 per troy ounce, up 1.08% from the $63.55 it cost on Friday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Recovery against US Dollar faces tariff risks – Commerzbank
item.description: Michael Pfister at Commerzbank highlights a strong Canadian labour market and improving Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) and exports as signs of real-economy recovery, but warns this is fragile due to threatened US tariffs.

item.title: Brent: Iran talks keep risk premium in focus – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists highlight that negotiations between Iran and Oman over a new shipping framework through the Strait of Hormuz remain finely balanced, with Tehran linking any lasting arrangement to broader demands on the US.
